---
title: "About"
---

This website explores how colonial land and forest laws shaped the making of Achimota Forest Reserve in the Gold Coast. It traces the legal path from land acquisition ordinances to the Forest Ordinance of 1927, showing how colonial officials used law to classify, regulate, and redesign land for conservation, education, sanitation, and urban improvement.

The project focuses on Achimota as a case study in colonial improvement. It argues that the Achimota Firewood Plantation and Forest Reserve were not simply environmental projects. They formed part of a wider plan to create a green buffer for Accra, supply fuel for Achimota School, support colonial education, and reorganize a landscape that already carried Ga meanings of land, sacredness, frontier settlement, and social marginality.

This digital project brings together ordinances, forestry reports, maps, archival images, and secondary scholarship to show how law transformed land into a reserve, and how Achimota became a model space where forest conservation, public health, education, and colonial authority met.
